clue.text: Finished digging? My congratulations!

definitions.meaning: playfully, a well that has been completely dug is finished
an exclamation of praise for a job handled nicely

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a spot of gardening and is warmly congratulated.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: digging a shaft for water is digging a well, so finishing it means the well is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idiomatic: completed (of a dug shaft, punningly) and the stock phrase of praise for an achievement.

clue.text: See 10
Over 50 in substantial English force

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: the Roman numeral sits in the word for substantial, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: substantial means big
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A description of a large English army with over fifty members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like a noun for a body of troops, but it is the verb, as in to compel someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To oblige someone is to compel or require them to act, a synonym of the verb force.

clue.text: Young lady's cheating boyfriend finally kicked out (row overheard)

indicators.note: the closing letter of the boyfriend is expelled from the word for cheating

parts.note: cheating, as a noun, is fraud

indicators.note: points to the closing letter of the word boyfriend
the word for row is taken as it sounds when listened to

parts.note: a row is a line, as of seats or people

explanation.surface: A young woman has a heard-about quarrel after her two-timing boyfriend is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally kicked out' removes D (end of boyfriend) from FRAUD, leaving FRAU; 'overheard' makes LEIN sound like LINE. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fräulein is the German title for an unmarried young woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Old girl's an unexpectedly key associate of 4

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly is out of its usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old girl is suddenly linked to some fourth person or thing.
explanation.walkthrough: On a standard keyboard the $ symbol shares a key with the digit 4, so it is that key's associate; the '4' looks like a cross-reference to 4 down but is just the digit.
explanation.definitionFit: On a typewriter or computer keyboard the currency symbol is typed by shifting the 4 key, so the two share a key.

clue.text: Hello admits shocking treatment — celeb initially furious

indicators.note: the greeting lets the treatment in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hi is an informal hello
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, literally a shock treatment

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of the word celeb

explanation.surface: A celebrity magazine reports on electric shock therapy, and some star is livid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hello' suggests the British celebrity magazine Hello!, but here it is just HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious can mean frantic or frenzied, as in a furious pace, which is what a hectic schedule is.

clue.text: Blame guy for disruption — pest!

indicators.note: the two words are to be disrupted, thrown out of their order, to give a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is blaming a fellow for causing a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A mealybug is a small sap-sucking insect with a powdery coat, a familiar pest of greenhouse plants.

clue.text: Flipping sniffer dog slips lead but doesn't give up

indicators.note: flipping turns the combined pieces over, so they are read backwards

parts.note: a sniffer is slang for the nose

indicators.note: the dog gets out of its lead, so the word dog loses its leading letter

parts.note: taken as the word dog

explanation.surface: An annoying sniffer dog escapes its leash but carries on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British curse on the dog, but it reverses NOSE + OG (DOG without its first letter) to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on is to continue or persist, the idiom for not stopping or quitting.

clue.text: Keeping Iron Cross under cover

indicators.note: the cross keeps the metal within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix, especially one in a church
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: The Iron Cross, a German military medal, is being kept hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Cross' reads as one name, the German medal, but the two words do separate jobs; a rood is the large crucifix in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Something roofed has a top over it, so it is sheltered or protected from above.

clue.text: Policy reversal — what's afoot?

definitions.meaning: a sudden change to the opposite position, a U-turn
a cryptic way of asking what is on one's foot: a rubber sandal held by a toe thong

explanation.surface: A political commentator asks what is going on after a government U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's afoot?' idiomatically means 'what is happening?', but literally it is what is on a foot: the sandal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a politician's about-turn and a cheap thong sandal worn on the beach.

clue.text: In yet another way, describing queen the greatest example of this?

definitions.text: In yet another way, describing queen the greatest example of this?

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the rearranged word surrounds the other pieces
putting the word yet another way means rearranging its letters

parts.note: Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a queen, the greatest of all, exemplifies some disparity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another way' rearranges the word yet into ETY. Read whole, a queen ranked above everyone is itself an instance of the thing defined; Ali famously called himself The Greatest.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch placed above all subjects illustrates unevenness of status, the lack of parity the word describes.

clue.text: Force to cut back — cool

indicators.note: the word for cut is run back, read from right to left

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
ice means to cool, as in icing a drink

explanation.surface: An instruction to reduce budgets and keep calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' is the noun here, as in a police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A police service is commonly called a force, as in the Metropolitan Police Force.

clue.text: Beset by trouble, one's bordering on careless almost

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is a link meaning is
to be next to something is to border on it

indicators.note: almost means the word for careless stops one letter short

parts.note: remiss means careless or negligent

explanation.surface: A troubled person is said to be close to recklessness.
explanation.walkthrough: REMISS loses its final S to become REMIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in extreme difficulty or danger, especially at the point of death.

clue.text: Making good progress over puzzle finally — tend to be a far from lateral thinker

indicators.note: the progress phrase goes over the letter, covering it, so the letter sits within

parts.note: being on track means progressing as planned

indicators.note: points to the closing letter of the word puzzle

parts.note: to mind is to look after or tend

explanation.surface: Advice to a solver who is getting on well with the puzzle, but lacks imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means covering: the progress phrase wraps round the last letter of puzzle. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obsessed with one subject thinks narrowly rather than laterally, the opposite of creative sideways thinking.

clue.text: Henry going: 'The price is different and this might prove it'

indicators.note: the remaining letters are made different, rearranged into a new order
the abbreviation for Henry leaves, taken out of the words before the anagram

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry departs, insisting the cost was not as stated and he has evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' removes H from THE PRICE to leave TEPRICE, which 'is different' rearranges. The definition refers back to a price paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip given at a sale is the evidence that a payment was made, so it proves the price.

clue.text: Our great leader shortly to reveal this dishonest scheme

parts.words: Our great leader shortly to reveal this
parts.note: BoJo, nickname of Boris Johnson, then UK prime minister, shortened is BOJ; the answer read as an instruction, put the word job up (written upward in a down entry), reveals it

explanation.surface: A sarcastic remark that the prime minister is about to unveil some scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction, PUT UP JOB, gives BOJ, a short form of BoJo, the nickname of then UK prime minister Boris Johnson. 'Great' is sarcastic.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud arranged beforehand, often to look like something else, is the idiom for a rigged plan.

clue.text: Ancient city, or a new one adopted by charity

indicators.note: the charity takes in the numeral, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Toc H is a British Christian charity founded after the First World War
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clue offering an ancient city, or else a newer one taken up by a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: TOC H is a British charitable movement founded in 1915; it takes in I to give TIOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a great city of the ancient world, in what is now southern Turkey.

clue.text: City which's announced bid

parts.note: the words which's sound like witches; a group of witches is a coven
a bid is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: A city that has made a public bid, perhaps to host an event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which's announced' sounds like 'witches', and a gathering of witches is a COVEN. Coventry is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry is a cathedral city in the West Midlands of England.

clue.text: Bill claims Republican is irritating

indicators.note: the billionaire takes hold of the abbreviation, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Bill Gates is the founder of Microsoft

explanation.surface: A political story: Bill alleges that a Republican is being annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like an invoice or a law, but it is Bill Gates.
explanation.definitionFit: To grate on someone is to irritate or annoy them, as a harsh sound does.

clue.text: Detective Murphy talking — he's in sole charge

indicators.note: the words are spoken, so their sound gives the entry

parts.note: a dick is slang for a detective; a murphy is old slang for a potato, a tater

explanation.surface: A detective called Murphy speaks up, saying he alone is in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murphy' looks like a surname but is an old slang word for a potato, from its association with Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocratic ruler holds absolute power alone, answerable to no one.

clue.text: Setter rolling in money mostly keeps working — not being serious!

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I

indicators.note: the shortened word keeps the other inside it
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: someone rolling in money is rich
on means working or operating, as a machine is

explanation.surface: A wealthy crossword setter keeps working, but only in jest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the wealth word to RIC before it keeps the working word inside; setters often call themselves I.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony says one thing while meaning another, so an ironic remark is not meant literally or earnestly.

clue.text: City have negligible backing? Not entirely!

indicators.note: the letters are taken backing, that is read from right to left
only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a city has hardly any support, and is told only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters AVENEG run through 'have negligible' and read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a Swiss city on Lake Geneva, home to many international bodies.

clue.text: Shut up a second! B___ stopping? I hope he is

indicators.note: the letters stop up the gag, sitting inside it

parts.note: to gag someone is to shut them up
the letter B stands for itself, the dashes a censored expletive

explanation.surface: An exasperated listener shouts at a bore, swearing, wishing he would stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the start of the clue: a windbag is someone you hope is stopping, that is, shutting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome talker who goes on and on is the sort of person one hopes will fall silent.

clue.text: Quack, quack! Duck walks in at the start

indicators.note: the word for in is placed at the front of the other pieces

parts.note: being in means being at home
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O
walks are paths

explanation.surface: A duck waddles in, quacking, at the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quack, quack!' sounds like a duck, but means two charlatans: the plural definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeopathy is widely regarded as pseudoscience, so its practitioners are often dismissed as charlatans.

clue.text: See 14
The last, not the first — great

indicators.note: the opening letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheerful remark that it is great to be last rather than first.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is slang for excellent or huge, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Desire for union to accept current offer, see

indicators.note: the exclamation takes in the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: lo is an archaic exclamation meaning look or see
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a bid is an offer

explanation.surface: A trade union wants to accept a pay offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union, but the union is sexual.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual drive, a craving for physical coupling.

clue.text: Shocks skinhead graffiti artists

parts.note: the head of skin, its first letter
taggers spray their signature tags on walls

explanation.surface: Skinhead graffiti vandals cause outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' is read as skin's head, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or shock them, a verb synonym.
